title: Temasek Holdings' Planned Restructuring and Potential Impact on Investment Performance and Returns
what_it_is: Temasek Holdings' Planned Restructuring and Potential Impact on Investment Performance and Returns

sections.label: Government oversight of Temasek
sections.summary: The Government ensures Temasek has a competent board but does not influence its individual investment decisions, and Temasek does not use a conventional reference portfolio.

sentences.text: The Government ensures that Temasek has a competent board to oversee its management but does not otherwise influence or direct Temasek's individual investment decisions.

With regard to Question No 14 on whether Temasek has any performance benchmarks, I had addressed this in the earlier reply; but in short, Temasek does not operate against a specific conventional reference portfolio as it is a direct investor, an investor that is bottom-up.

sections.label: No strategic development requirement
sections.summary: Beyond oversight of its investments, Temasek is not required to pursue specific strategic or economic development strategies.

sentences.text: Beyond exercising the appropriate oversight over its investments, there is no requirement for Temasek to pursue specific strategic or economic development strategies.

sections.label: Board accountable for long-term returns
sections.summary: The Government holds Temasek's board accountable for good long-term returns on net portfolio performance after deducting all investment fees and expenses.

sentences.text: Ultimately, the Government holds the board of Temasek accountable for delivering good long-term returns on its overall portfolio and that is on the basis of net portfolio performance, after deducting all investment fees and expenses.

sections.label: Unlisted assets and risk premium
sections.summary: Unlisted assets should by definition generate higher returns because they carry a risk premium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: As for the difference between listed and unlisted assets, well, unlisted assets, by definition, should generate higher returns because they have a risk premium associated with them.

sections.label: Comparison with other sovereign funds
sections.summary: Temasek's performance has been commensurate with higher-risk sovereign wealth funds such as the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, both achieving 20-year annualised total shareholder returns of about 8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Nonetheless, as a comparison, I think Temasek's performance has, indeed, been commensurate with other sovereign wealth funds with a higher risk profile, such as the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Just as a comparison, both have achieved 20-year annualised total shareholder returns of about 8%.

sections.label: Dividend spending and asset proportions
sections.summary: The Government will not go into how dividends are spent or what proportion of listed or unlisted assets should be managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Beyond that, we will not go into exactly how the dividends are spent and what proportion of listed or unlisted assets they should manage.
